paras: The attack on the funeral of A. Oscar Jones was a street assault in Philadelphia in late February or early March 1881, in which boys stoned Black mourners in the funeral procession of the captain of the Grey Invincibles, a Black militia company. A running fight with stones and pistol shots followed until police quelled the crowd; no serious injuries were reported.

Alonzo Oscar Jones had been captain of the Gray Invincibles of the Pennsylvania National Guard, and a People's Advocate correspondent praised him for "raising the standard of his race as militia men in his native State." His funeral was "very largely attended," with militia deputations and thronged streets along the route.

When the cortege reached Broad and Catherine streets, "a party of boys threw a stone at some colored people who were riding in carriages," according to a Philadelphia dispatch. Several of the Black men jumped from the carriages and tried to seize the person who had thrown it, and the crowds on the street joined in. From there to the cemetery at Passyunk avenue, west of Broad street, a general fight continued along the line of march, with stones thrown and pistol shots fired. The dispatch names neither the shooters nor the race of the boys and crowd.

Lieutenant Warnock of the First district and a squad of police quelled the mob and protected the returning procession; no one was seriously injured "so far as could be ascertained." No report of arrests or prosecutions appears in the coverage.

The attack is known from one wire item datelined Philadelphia, March 1, printed by the Wheeling Daily Intelligencer on March 2 under the headline "Attack on a Funeral by a Mob" and naming the mourners only as "colored people," without comment on motive. The People's Advocate of Washington, a Black-edited weekly, printed a tribute to Jones and an account of the funeral on March 5 that mentions no disturbance.
The date is uncertain: the dispatch is datelined March 1, while the People's Advocate correspondent dated the funeral "Sunday 27th inst.," which would place the attack on February 27.

accounts.label: Wire report (Philadelphia, March 1)
accounts.gist: Boys threw a stone at colored mourners at Broad and Catherine; mourners tried to catch the thrower, crowds joined, and a fight with stones and pistol shots ran to the cemetery until police quelled the mob; no one seriously injured.

accounts.label: People's Advocate correspondent
accounts.gist: The funeral on Sunday the 27th was very largely attended, with militia deputations and thronged streets; no disturbance is mentioned.

framing.detail: The Wheeling Intelligencer ran the Philadelphia dispatch under 'Attack on a Funeral by a Mob', calling the street crowd 'the mob' and noting no serious injuries, without comment (A1, A2).
The Black-edited People's Advocate eulogized Jones for 'raising the standard of his race as militia men' and described a well-attended funeral without mentioning any attack (A3).

versions.value: Dispatch datelined Philadelphia, March 1 (event date not stated in the text)

conflicts.note: The wire dateline is likely the filing date rather than the funeral date; the People's Advocate, a correspondent's account, dates the funeral to Sunday the 27th ('inst.' printed, February meant, since the paper ran March 5). The attack itself is reported only in the wire item.
